title: Co-ownership disputes - partition vs sale by mutual consent
p1:
Two siblings inherit the same property. One wants to sell, the other wants to keep it. Who gets the final say?

Many people assume that owning a share of a property means they can use or sell the entire property. That is not how co-ownership works.
p2:
A co-owner can usually deal with their own share, but not the whole property without agreement from others. When disagreements arise, there are two common paths: partition or sale by mutual consent.

Partition means dividing the property so each owner gets a separate share. Sale by mutual consent means all owners agree to sell the property and divide the proceeds.
p3:
The surprising part? A property does not always have to be physically divided. If division is impractical, selling the property and sharing the money may be the more practical solution.

The best approach depends on the property type, relationships between owners, and willingness to cooperate. Clear communication early can prevent years of disputes.
conclusion: If co-owners cannot agree on keeping a property together, would you prefer partition or a mutual sale? What factors would influence your choice?
